newsitem.title: UK: Ex-archbishop calls Princess Diana actress-schemer.
newsitem.headline: Ex-archbishop calls Princess Diana actress-schemer.

text.p: The former head of the Church of England has described Princess Diana as an actress and a schemer but says he feels concerned for her future.
Robert Runcie, onetime Archbishop of Canterbury, also said he knew about her husband Prince Charles' relationship with old flame Camilla Parker Bowles before it surfaced publicly.
Runcie, who married the now-divorced couple at St Paul's Cathedral in 1981, said he believed it was an arranged marriage about which Charles was very depressed.
In a series of taped interviews for a biography released on Monday, Runcie said he saw early cracks in the royal marriage well before they became public.

Speaking about Diana's grandmother Lady Ruth Fermoy, he said "Ruth was very distressed with Diana's behaviour...She (Ruth) was totally and wholly a Charles person...and regarded Diana as an actress, a schemer -- all of which is true, of course."
"I don't know what will become of her. Sad, really, and I feel a desire to suppport her," Runcie added.
Heir to the throne Charles will become Supreme Governor of the Church of England when he succeeds Queen Elizabeth.

The interviews were recorded three years ago, before Charles and Diana were divorced last month. Their marriage and bitter breakup remain a major source of fascination for Britons and Runcie's comments received front-page coverage.
Runcie recalled meeting the couple with his chaplain Richard Chartres to discuss their wedding arrangements. "Richard said to me "He's (Charles) seriously depressed. You can tell from his voice.'"
"We thought it was an arranged marriage but my view was, "They're a nice couple and she'll grow into it'," said Runcie.
Runcie said he knew about Charles' then-secret relationship with Parker Bowles - blamed by many Britons in part for the marital breakup - and added:
"That was what worried Ruth Fermoy, about his needing a woman to love and be cared for by. And also that Diana would never be under control until she fell in love with someone."
Runcie, Archbishop of Canterbury from 1980 to 1991, has expressed unhappiness about what he calls private comments finding their way into the biography.
The book, "The Reluctant Archbishop", by Humphrey Carpenter to be published later in the year, contains a note from him saying "I have done my best to die before this book is published."
In a damaging section about Charles and his role as future king and Supreme Governor, Runcie said the prince was "disenchanted" with the Church.
"It would quite help if he loved the Church of England a bit more...I think he'd given up on the Church of England before I arrived," he said.

"I think he was deeply into the Laurens van der Post spirituality," said Runcie, referring to the British writer and explorer. "When it came to his concern to do something about the state of the country, I don't think he took the Church of England very seriously."
"Charles is highly sensitive...But he is a mass of contradictions... He hunts regularly but is a great man about the environment. So that the public don't really know where they are," he said.
A glamorous mother of two, Diana is one of the most photographed women in the world and has media popularity in Britain that has always eluded Charles, seen as aloof and a more awkward public figure.
